acceptance_criteria: Both endpoint evaluations return under the fixed settings for update 32 within wall_s 300 and prediction_evaluations 2.
The result reports endpoint tip speed for the recorded input and for the braking-box input plus their difference, and the endpoint position difference.

Materially lower braking-box endpoint speed at this state is reported as local braking authority being available; near-equal endpoint speeds are reported as locally bounded braking authority; neither outcome is reported as a dominant or causal settling explanation.
arguments.additional_need: Both projected endpoint speeds under matched settings, and whether the braking-box per-tendon force limits bind at this saved state.
discriminating_observations: Sign and magnitude of (recorded-input endpoint speed - braking-box endpoint speed) at this single saved state.
Whether the braking-box endpoint speed falls below the 0.02 m/s settling speed limit over this one 0.01 s step.
Endpoint position shift between the two arms, to check the braking box is not merely trading speed reduction for a large position penalty.
fixed_conditions: model.gvs@1.0.0, implicit_euler integration, integration step 0.002 s, horizon 0.01 s (host-fixed)
saved projected measured_initial_state bound to update 32 only; state vectors not restated here
recorded applied input = update 32 actual_tension_n, used as the comparison arm with no substitution
single execution scope; no backend re-execution and no closed-loop replay
hypotheses: H1_unused_local_braking: the recorded applied input for update 32 leaves locally available braking authority unused, so the braking-box input yields a materially lower projected endpoint tip speed at this saved state.

H2_locally_bounded_braking: braking authority at this saved state is locally bounded (per-tendon force limits, geometry, or projected-model limits), so the braking-box input yields an endpoint tip speed close to the recorded input's.

H3_same_local_endpoint_from_different_mechanisms: if the two endpoints differ, objective weighting (terminal/holding tip-speed weights recorded as 0.0) and solver early-stop plan quality both predict the same local outcome and cannot be separated by this probe.
arguments.local_question: At the saved projected state bound to update 32 (t=0.32 s, the sampled late interval with the fastest reconstructed tip speed, measured_speed 1.5810 m/s), does an instantaneous braking-box input over the host-fixed 0.01 s horizon yield a lower projected endpoint tip speed than the recorded applied input for that same update?
metrics: projected endpoint tip speed under the recorded applied input (m/s)
projected endpoint tip speed under the instantaneous braking-box input (m/s)
endpoint tip speed difference, recorded minus braking-box (m/s)
unresolved: This probe cannot separate objective weighting (recorded terminal_tip_speed_weight and holding_tip_speed_weight 0.0) from solver early-stop plan quality when both predict the same local endpoint.
This probe cannot test projected-GVS versus backend-model mismatch, because both arms are evaluated with the projected model.

Independent limit of outcome: a single 0.01 s saved-state comparison cannot explain, rank, or attribute the whole closed-loop settling failure, and no closed-loop counterfactual replay or causal-attribution capability is available in this inventory.
